neighbours.label: the continuation after conceding a difficulty ('hard, but it's worth it'): the other side of the + pole's 'harder than it looks'
fire: Training a puppy takes patience, but it pays off within weeks.
The climb to the summit is exhausting, but the view makes it worthwhile.
Quitting sugar is never easy but small steps go a long way.
Writing a thesis is a long slog, but you will get there.
Moving abroad was scary, but it's the best thing I ever did.
Raising twins is hard work but it's incredibly rewarding.
Learning to code can feel overwhelming, but anyone can do it.
Saving money on a small salary is tough, but it is doable.
quiet: The shop sells apples, but it also sells fresh bread.
My brother likes tea, but my sister prefers coffee.
The hotel was near the beach but far from the station.
He called on Monday, but she was out of town.
The car is blue, but the truck is red.
The museum opens at nine, but the café opens at eight.
The book is short, but it has many photographs.
Paris is in France, but Geneva is in Switzerland.

notes: + pole: 'not as easy as it looks'; - pole: concession that the hard thing is still doable/worth it.
